1	// Subprocess helpers for andesim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.
7	#ifndef ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <functional>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <string_view>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	struct RunResult {
18	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
19	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
20	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
21	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
22	};
23	
24	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
25	// is redirected to /dev/null; stderr too, unless relay_stderr is set, in
26	// which case the child inherits OUR stderr and its diagnostics stream live
27	// (used to surface the legs' leveled logs at --log-level <= debug). If the
28	// child runs longer than timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
29	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms,
30	                      bool relay_stderr = false);
31	
32	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
33	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
34	// `run --mode fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
35	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
36	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
37	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
38	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
39	
40	// Fork a child that execs argv with inherited stdio and return immediately
41	// without waiting. Used by `run --mode cycle --gdb` to launch vsim in the
42	// background before exec-ing ICEman in the foreground. Returns the child pid
43	// on success, -1 on empty argv or fork failure.
44	int fork_background(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
45	
46	// Run argv with BOTH stdout and stderr captured (separate pipes) and stdin
47	// inherited, streaming each complete line to `on_line(stream, line)` as it
48	// arrives -- stream is 1 (stdout) or 2 (stderr), line excludes the trailing
49	// newline. The callback owns presentation (it decides what to write to the real
50	// streams), so this is the filtered counterpart to exec_passthrough: same "run
51	// to completion, no timeout, propagate exit code" contract, but the parent sees
52	// every line. A final unterminated line is delivered too. Returns the child's
53	// exit code, 128+signal if signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
54	int run_line_filtered(
55	    const std::vector<std::string>& argv,
56	    const std::function<void(int stream, std::string_view line)>& on_line);
57	
58	}  // namespace andes_sim
59	
60	#endif  // ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
27	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
28	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
29	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
30	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
31	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
32	
33	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
34	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
35	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
36	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
37	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
38	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
39	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
40	
41	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
42	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
43	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
44	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
45	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
46	
47	// Returns {st_value, st_value + st_size} for the FUNC symbol covering `addr`.
48	// Both members are 0 when not found or unreadable.
49	std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> fn_range(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- there is no QEMU2 handback leg.
2	// run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	#include "process.hpp"
18	
19	namespace andes_sim {
20	
21	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
22	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
23	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
24	struct RuntimeCtx {
25	  std::string mmap_path;
26	  long long mem_size = 0;
27	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
28	  std::string plugin_path;
29	  // QEMU `-readconfig` file matching the accurate engine's ISA, distilled from
30	  // its config.inc (the engine's `--print-qemu-config`). Empty => the fast leg
31	  // keeps its descriptor's default `-cpu` (engines without the flag; FA2).
32	  std::string qemu_cfg;
33	  // The QEMU CPU model the fast leg must instantiate ({qemu_cpu} fill),
34	  // parsed from the same probe's `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` globals: the
35	  // readconfig globals only apply to THAT driver, and a mismatched model
36	  // silently ignores them (found live: andes-ax45mpv kept vlen=512 when the
37	  // ax66 run asked for 128). Empty => the family default (andes-ax45mpv).
38	  std::string qemu_cpu;
39	};
40	
41	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
42	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
43	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
44	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
45	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
46	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
47	}
48	
49	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
50	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
51	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
52	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
53	// themselves).
54	struct LegTriggerArgs {
55	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
56	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
57	};
58	
59	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
60	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. Roles other
61	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
62	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
63	//
64	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
65	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
66	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
67	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
68	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
69	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
70	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
71	                                std::string& err);
72	
73	// Turn an accurate engine's `<bin> --print-qemu-config` probe into a QEMU
74	// `-readconfig` file under `workdir`. On a clean probe (exit 0, non-empty
75	// stdout) writes `workdir/qemu.cfg` and returns its path; on any failure
76	// (engine without the flag -> the parser throws -> non-zero exit; timeout;
77	// spawn failure; empty output; unwritable dir) returns "" -- the tolerant
78	// fallback that leaves the fast leg on its descriptor's default -cpu.
79	std::string stage_qemu_cfg(const std::string& workdir, const RunResult& probe);
80	
81	// The QEMU CPU model named by a `--print-qemu-config` probe's text: the first
82	// `driver = "<cpu>-riscv-cpu"` global, stripped of the "-riscv-cpu" suffix.
83	// "" when the text names none (probe failed / engine without the hook) -- the
84	// caller falls back to the family-default -cpu.
85	std::string qemu_cpu_from_cfg(const std::string& cfg_text);
86	
87	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
88	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
89	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
90	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
91	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
92	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
93	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
94	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
95	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
96	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
97	
98	// The exit code a leg returns after draining its state and handing off (the
99	// driver-side mirror of vsim's kExitHandoffToQemu). Every plan step is a drain
100	// step, so this is the expected per-leg exit.
101	constexpr int kDrainRc = 200;
102	
103	struct PlanOptions {
104	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
105	  int expect_rc = kDrainRc;   // drain success code
106	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
107	  bool dry_run = false;       // build argvs (incl. qemu_cfg) but spawn nothing
108	};
109	
110	// Compose the "plan step N exited wrong" diagnostic. A drain step (expect_rc is
111	// the handoff/drain code) that exits 0 ran the ELF to completion without ever
112	// reaching its ROI boundary -- the marker/pc trigger never fired; say so and
113	// name the trigger kind so the fix (right ELF / right --trigger) is obvious.
114	// Any other mismatch gets the plain "expected X, got Y" line.
115	std::string plan_step_rc_error(size_t step, const Step& s, int expect_rc,
116	                               int got_rc);
117	
118	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
119	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
120	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
121	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
122	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
123	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
124	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
125	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
126	
127	}  // namespace andes_sim
128	
129	#endif  // ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

1	// andesim leveled logging.
2	//
3	// The scale mirrors the vsim engines' --log-level option so users learn one
4	// scheme: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off. A message
5	// prints when its level >= the threshold; the default threshold is info.
6	//
7	// What lives at which level (driver policy):
8	//   info  -- the answers: program output relays, the cycle figure,
9	//            --dry-run/--verify results. Program output itself is never
10	//            gated (it is the program's, not a log).
11	//   debug -- driver chatter: the hybrid banner, the mmap line, PASS lines,
12	//            verify progress notes.
13	//   warn  -- degradations: unsupported-CSR warnings, skipped engines.
14	// Fatal errors are not gated: they accompany a non-zero exit.
15	#ifndef ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
16	#define ANDESIM_LOG_HPP
17	
18	#include <string>
19	
20	namespace andes_sim {
21	
22	enum LogLevel {
23	  kLogTrace = 0,
24	  kLogDebug = 1,
25	  kLogInfo = 2,
26	  kLogWarn = 3,
27	  kLogError = 4,
28	  kLogCritical = 5,
29	  kLogOff = 6,
30	};
31	
32	// Set the process-wide threshold from the CLI value. "" keeps the default
33	// (info). Returns false (and leaves the threshold alone) when the value is
34	// not an integer in 0..6.
35	bool set_log_threshold(const std::string& cli_value);
36	
37	// The current threshold (0..6). Used to forward the level to child engines.
38	int log_threshold();
39	
40	// True when a message at `level` should print.
41	bool log_on(int level);
42	
43	// Open the --log-file sink. Once open, EVERY log_line/log_result message --
44	// all levels, even below the console threshold -- is appended to the file
45	// with a UTC timestamp and a level tag. Returns false if the file cannot be
46	// opened (the sink stays off). Empty path is a no-op success.
47	bool set_log_file(const std::string& path);
48	
49	// The open sink's path, or "" when none.
50	const std::string& log_file_path();
51	
52	// Emit one chatter line to stderr when `level` passes the threshold. Pass
53	// the complete line text (including its "[andesim] " prefix), without the
54	// trailing newline. Always mirrored to the --log-file sink.
55	void log_line(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
56	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
57	
58	// Emit one RESULT line (the cycle figure, PASS/verify verdicts) to stdout
59	// when `level` passes the threshold. Always mirrored to the sink.
60	void log_result(int level, const char* fmt, ...)
61	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
62	
63	}  // namespace andes_sim
64	
65	#endif  // ANDESIM_LOG_HPP

#      answer --describe AND --print-qemu-config drive the real

#      QEMU command without spawning it, so every assertion is deterministic.

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"

# --print-qemu-config names CPU (a minimal but valid -readconfig text). An
# empty CPU makes the probe FAIL (exit 1), like an engine without the hook.
mkengine() {
  local f="$1/$2"

  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$3","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","xlen":64,"vlen":$4,"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]}}'
elif [ "\$1" = "--print-qemu-config" ]; then
  [ -n "$5" ] || exit 1
  printf '[global]\ndriver = "$5-riscv-cpu"\nproperty = "vlen"\nvalue = "$4"\n'
else
  echo "RAN:\$*"

  chmod +x "$f"

mkengine "$D2" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 "andes-ax45mpv"
mkengine "$D2" v2 "vsim:v2" 128 "andes-ax66"
mkengine "$DN" v1 "vsim:v1" 512 ""   # probe fails -> default -cpu, no -readconfig

# the engine-derived -cpu (model from the probe, vlen from --describe), the
# staged -readconfig, the plugin with default limit/min_iters, and -bios.

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"

  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --limit 7 --min-iters 3 "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-m 256M' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mem-size 256M "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-icount shift=0' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY" -- -icount shift=0
# 2c. two engines, no --engine: ambiguous, names both; --engine picks one and
# its OWN cpu/vlen pair follows (ax66 + vlen=128).
expect 2 'multiple cycle-accurate.*vsim:v1.*vsim:v2' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax66,vlen=128' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D2" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:v2 "$DUMMY"
# 2d. no cycle-accurate engine discoverable: the same clear error hybrid gives
expect 2 'no cycle-accurate engine' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$DE" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$DUMMY"
expect 2 "no engine 'vsim:nope'" \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:nope "$DUMMY"

# -cpu family, vlen still synced from --describe, and NO -readconfig.

  || fail "probe-less engine: missing default -cpu: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q -- '-readconfig' \
  && fail "probe-less engine: unexpected -readconfig: $out"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'no --print-qemu-config' \
  || fail "probe-less engine: missing the fallback warning: $out"
# 2f. CLI shape errors
expect 2 'missing ELF' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run
expect 2 'QEMU args go after --' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run a.elf b.elf
expect 2 'ELF not found' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run "$TMP/nope.elf"
# 2g. run-only flags are rejected loudly, not silently ignored
expect 2 'not a profile option' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --trigger marker "$DUMMY"
expect 2 'not a profile option' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --mode fast "$DUMMY"
expect 2 'not a profile option' \
  env ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$D1" "$BIN" profile --dry-run --verify "$DUMMY"
# 2h. profile appears in the help tree
expect 0 'profile' "$BIN" --help
expect 0 'profile' "$BIN" profile --help
echo "[ok] fake-engine profile: engine-derived cfg, errors, dry-run argv"

# 3. real engine (guarded, still --dry-run): the staged cfg + cpu come from the
# actual sim_ax45mpv_premium probe.
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
if [ -x "$SIM" ]; then
  expect 0 '\-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=[0-9]+' \
    "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
  expect 0 '\-readconfig .*/qemu\.cfg' \
    "$BIN" profile --dry-run --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
  echo "[ok] real engine probe: -cpu/-readconfig derived from sim_ax45mpv_premium"
else
  echo "[skip] real engine layer: no built $SIM"
fi

ok "profile: engine-synced QEMU profile command"

Review complete. The new driver code actually reuses the heavy orchestration seams well (`discover_engines`/`resolve_accurate_engine`/`elf_engine_arch_error`/`builtin_qemu_arch`/`stage_qemu_cfg`/`qemu_cpu_from_cfg`/`synced_vlen`/`print_dry_run`/`render_argv`/`run_process`/`exec_passthrough`/`log_line`, plus `config_env_value` and `symbolize`/`fn_range`); the profile and hvm-wiring shell tests correctly source `tests/lib/log.sh` + `paths.sh`. The reuse gaps are in the smaller re-inlined utilities.

## Findings

1. **cmd_profile.cpp:304-308 — the absolute-existing-ELF preflight re-inlines cmd_run.cpp's `abs_elf`.**
   Cost: `fs::absolute(...)` + `!fs::is_regular_file(...)` → "ELF not found" is a second copy of the exact preflight at `driver/cmd_run.cpp:54-68` (`abs_elf`), which the header comment there advertises as "the one resolver fast/cycle/cycle-gdb share" — profile is a fourth standalone-ELF command that pointedly does not share it. The profile code comment (line 304-305) even says "the same up-front check run's abs_elf does."
   Existing helper: `abs_elf(path, ctx)` in `driver/cmd_run.cpp:54`. It already returns the resolved abs string and already takes a `ctx` label; the only thing blocking a drop-in is the hardcoded "andesim run" literal in its message (line 58/63). Fix = hoist `abs_elf` to a shared header and generalize that prefix, then call it from `cmd_profile.cpp` instead of the inline block.

2. **cmd_profile.cpp:388-394 — inline whole-file slurp duplicates `read_file`.**
   Cost: `std::ifstream f(...); std::stringstream ss; ss << f.rdbuf(); log_text = ss.str();` is the same ifstream+rdbuf→string idiom as `read_file` at `driver/engine_registry.cpp:101-106` (and a twin in cmd_doctor.cpp). Low severity.
   Existing helper: `read_file(path)` in `driver/engine_registry.cpp:101` — but it is file-local (anonymous namespace), so reuse means hoisting it to a shared header first. If not hoisted, this is a "pick one home" nit rather than a call-site swap.

## Non-findings (duplication exists but no existing helper genuinely fits)

3. **cmd_profile.cpp:56-73 `cmd_exists`/`find_first` vs cmd_doctor.cpp:125-141 `which`** — the PATH-walk-with-`::access(...,X_OK)` loop overlaps, but `cmd_exists` must also accept `/`-containing candidates (the `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-...-objdump` absolute paths in `resolve_objdump`), which `which()` cannot resolve (it only PATH-walks bare names). Different semantics; `which()` is not a drop-in. (Both are also file-local.)

4. **cmd_profile.cpp:93-145 `capture_with_stdin`** — no existing helper writes to a child's stdin; `run_process` sends `/dev/null` and `run_line_filtered` inherits stdin (`driver/process.hpp:29,54`). Genuinely new. (Its `execvp`+`_exit(127)` / `waitpid` mirror process.cpp's file-local `exec_or_die`/`wait_for_exit_code`, but those aren't exported.)

5. **cmd_profile.cpp:240-255 `Workdir` (RAII mkdtemp)** — the only other mkdtemp is inline in `run_plan.cpp:359-371`, and it is keep-on-failure (evidence) rather than auto-remove, and never factored into a helper. No shared tempdir helper exists.

6. **profile.cpp:23 `appendf`** — no existing string-append formatter; `strutil.hpp` has only `ljust`/`join`/`vlen_str`, and `log.cpp` formats into fixed buffers. Genuinely new.

7. **cmd_profile.cpp:224-236 `parse_knob`** — no existing positive-int parser; `log.cpp`'s `set_log_threshold` is 0..6-specific. Genuinely new.

8. **Fake-engine JSON repeated across test_andes_sim_profile.sh:38-52, test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh:44-52, test_andes_sim_hvm_wiring.sh:53-57** — real 3-way duplication, but there is no shared fake-engine helper anywhere to reuse; `tests/lib/` has none and `f2/f3/f8/f9/print_qemu_config` all hand-roll the same `--describe`/`--print-qemu-config` shell scripts. Nothing existing to call.

9. **test_plugin_hotIterationLoop_measure.sh does not source `tests/lib/log.sh`** (hand-rolls `{ echo "FAIL[...]"; exit 1; }` and `SKIP: … exit 0`). Its deleted predecessor didn't either, and plugin-test siblings are split (~7 source log.sh; several use this bespoke `FAIL[name]:`/`SKIP:`-exit-0 idiom that `log.sh`'s `fail`/`ok` do not model). Consistent with the existing convention; not a regression this diff introduced.

10. **`"andes-ax45mpv"` family-default literal at cmd_profile.cpp:343 duplicates run_plan.cpp:296** — a repeated magic string, but there is no existing named constant for the CPU model (`kQemuId64/32` cover engine ids only), so there is no helper/constant to reuse.
